```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(ipumsr)      # used to read IPUMS extracts
#library(plyr)        # used for ddply to calculate some within HH variables
library(dplyr)       # used for data-cleaning and filtering
library(tidyverse)  #used to reshape long to wide on some variables


# Load project configuration
source(here::here("R", "load_config.R"))
cfg <- load_config()

# Define IPUMS input files 2019
ipums_2019 <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$input_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$input_2019
)


# Define IPUMS input files 2022
ipums_2022_1year <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$input_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$input_2022_1year
)

ipums_2022_5year <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$input_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$input_2022_5year
)

# Define IPUMS input file 2024
ipums_2024_1year <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$input_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$input_2024_1year
)

ipums_2024_5year <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$input_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$input_2024_5year
)

stopifnot(file.exists(ipums_2022_1year))
stopifnot(file.exists(ipums_2022_5year))
stopifnot(file.exists(ipums_2024_1year))
stopifnot(file.exists(ipums_2024_5year))

```

## Load 2019 data single year data

```{r}

ddi <-read_ipums_ddi(ipums_2019)


year_check <- read_ipums_micro(
  ddi,
  vars = "YEAR"
)

## check it is the right year before we even fully load the dataset
years <- unique(year_check$YEAR)

if (!all(years == 2019)) {
  stop(
    sprintf(
      "Expected YEAR=2022. Found: %s",
      paste(sort(years), collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}

#load the full dataset
ipums_data <- read_ipums_micro(ddi)

# Only work with housing units (TYPEHUGQ ==1)
# So, we are excluding group quarters (TYPEHUGQ == 2 and TYPEHUGQ 3)
# also limiting to San Diego county

data<- ipums_data %>% 
  filter(GQ == 1,
         COUNTYFIP==73,
         YEAR == 2019)

# Confirming state and county only San Diego and CA and that our GQ filter worked

stopifnot(all(data$STATEFIP == 6))
stopifnot(all(data$COUNTYFIP==73))
stopifnot(all(data$GQ==1))

# getting rid of statefips, countyfips, group quarters 
# all observations are now identical for these variables 
# the replication weights are not needed for complex survey design 
data <- data %>%
  select(-starts_with("REPWT"), -STATEFIP, -COUNTYFIP, -GQ)

## create a subset for HH data to join later
data_HH <- subset(data, select = c(HHWT, PERNUM, PERWT, SERIAL, HHINCOME,AGE, RACE, RACED, SEX, HHTYPE, RELATE, RELATED, EMPSTAT, LABFORCE))

### Household data: size, child present, senior present, and income cat ###

# Number of HH members, HHSize
# Every person in the same household, ie. sharing the same SERIALNO
HHSize <- data_HH %>%
  dplyr::group_by(SERIAL) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(HHSize = n())

data <- data %>% right_join(HHSize, by=c("SERIAL"))
rm(HHSize)
 
# Presence of children, ChildPresent
# Census def of children: All persons under 18, excluding people
# who maintain households, families, or subfamilies as
# a reference person or spouse

# For us, there is a children present (ChildPresent ==1) if
# there is at least one person under 18 who is not a reference person or spouse
# If no one meets these characteristics,
# then there is no child present (ChildPresent ==0)

HHChild <- subset(data_HH, select = c(SERIAL, RELATE, AGE)) %>%
  mutate(
    IsChild = if_else(
      !(RELATE %in% c(1, 2)) & AGE < 18,
      1,
      0
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(SERIAL) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    ChildPresent = max(IsChild, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

data<- data %>% right_join(HHChild, by=c("SERIAL"))
rm(HHChild)

# Presence of 65+ (inclusive), SeniorPresent
# 0 no, 1 yes

HHSenior <- subset(data_HH, select = c(SERIAL, AGE)) %>%
  mutate(SeniorPresent = if_else(AGE>=65,1,0)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(SERIAL) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(SeniorPresent = max(SeniorPresent, na.rm=TRUE))

data <- data %>% right_join(HHSenior, by=c("SERIAL"))
rm(HHSenior )

# Labor force (LF)
# 0 no, 1 yes
# Assume in LF if age between 16 and 70 and in labor force,
# LABFORCE codes 0 = N/A, 1 = no, 2 yes, 9 = unknown 

data <- data %>%
  mutate(LF = if_else((AGE>=16 & AGE<=70) & LABFORCE==2, 1, 0 ))

 

# Sex
# original coding 1 = male 2 = female 9 = missing blank
# recoding 0 female, 1 male

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(SEX = if_else(SEX == 1, 1, 0))

# Age categories
# Category 1: less than 15, Category 2: 15 (inclusive) to 25,
# Category 3: 25 (inclusive) to 70, Category 4: 70 and older

data <- data %>%
  mutate(AgeCode = case_when(AGE<15 ~ 1,
                    AGE>=15 & AGE<25 ~ 2,
                    AGE>=25 & AGE<70 ~ 3,
                    AGE>=70 ~ 4,
                    TRUE ~ NA))

### Compress into unique Households, HH ###

data<- data %>%
  filter(RELATE==1)

## create factor variables

# drop incomes less than zero 
data <- data %>% filter(HHINCOME > 0)

## san diego 2019 CPI =299.433
## san diego 2022 CPI = 344.416	
## 2019 * (2022cpi/2019cpi) = 2022 dollars

data <- data %>%
  mutate(ADJ_HHINCOME = HHINCOME*(344.416/299.433))

#establish where we are going to cut the continuous variable
cut_points <- c(0, 15000, 30000, 45000, 60000, 75000, 100000, 125000, 150000, 200000, 300000, 500000, 700000, 900000, Inf)
#there are 15 cut points and 14 categories, we could just set num_interval to 14
#but this way if we ever change the categories, it will auto adjust
num_intervals <- length(cut_points) - 1

#creates a series of labels Inc1, Inc2, Inc3,...,IncN N= # categories
incrementing_labels <- paste0("Inc", 1:num_intervals)

# creates the ordered factor variable Income_Cat left closed for each cut
data <- data %>%
  mutate(IncCat= cut(
    ADJ_HHINCOME, # the continuous variable being cut
    breaks = cut_points, # where to make the cuts
    labels = incrementing_labels, # how to label each bracket
    right = FALSE, # left close eg Inc1 is [0,15000) Inc2 [15000,30000)
    ordered_result = TRUE, # this is an ordered factor so Inc1< Inc2<...<Inc14
                 )
    ) # preserves the bucket variable after the next step


# Create the 14 binary columns (Inc1 to Inc14)  
dummies <- as.data.frame(model.matrix(~ IncCat - 1, data = data))

# Remove the "IncCat" prefix so column names are simply Inc1, Inc2, ..., Inc14
colnames(dummies) <- sub("^IncCat", "", colnames(dummies))

# Bind them to the dataset 
data <- bind_cols(data, dummies)


ACS_2019_1Y <- data  
# # Collapse into households, this keeps the first row of each SERIALNO
# HH <- data %>% distinct(SERIAL, .keep_all = TRUE)

rm(data, data_HH, ddi, ipums_data, years, year_check, dummies)




```

## create year mean variable for input into predictions
```{r}

## Multiply all variables by HHWT in the sample.  Even for head of HH, we care
# about how many such similarly headed households there are, not how many such
# people (PERWT) there are


years <- c(2019, 2022, 2024)

ACS_Means <- lapply(years, function(yr) {
  get(paste0("ACS_", yr, "_1Y")) %>%
    summarise(
      YEAR = first(YEAR),
      ADJ_HHINCOME = weighted.mean(ADJ_HHINCOME, HHWT),
      HHINCOME = weighted.mean(HHINCOME, HHWT),
      SeniorPresent = weighted.mean(SeniorPresent, HHWT),
      ChildPresent = weighted.mean(ChildPresent, HHWT),
      AGE = weighted.mean(AGE, HHWT),
      SEX = weighted.mean(SEX, HHWT),
      LF = weighted.mean(LF, HHWT),
      HHSize = weighted.mean(HHSize, HHWT),
      NHH = sum(HHWT)
    )
})


ACS_1year_means <-bind_rows(ACS_Means)


```


## Create observed bin counts from the ACS data by year

```{r}



years <- c(2019, 2022, 2024)

ACS_IncCat_Counts <- bind_rows(
  lapply(years, function(yr) {
    get(paste0("ACS_", yr, "_1Y")) %>%
      group_by(IncCat) %>%
      summarise(
        HH_Count = sum(HHWT, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(YEAR = yr)
  })
) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = IncCat,
    values_from = HH_Count
  ) %>%
  arrange(YEAR)


```


## Export CSV

```{r}

# Create output directory if it does not exist
dir.create(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# Construct output file path for 2019 1 year
output_2019 <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_2019_1year
)


# Write CSV
write.csv(
  ACS_2019_1Y,
  output_2019,
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Dataset saved to:", output_2019, "\n")

# Read the CSV back for verification
exported_data <- read.csv(output_2019)

# Verify dimensions and column names
stopifnot(
  nrow(exported_data) == nrow(ACS_2019_1Y),
  identical(names(exported_data), names(ACS_2019_1Y))
)

cat("Export verification passed.\n")
cat("Rows:", nrow(exported_data), "\n")
cat("Columns:", ncol(exported_data), "\n")
```
